title: compact hotpath: inline dequant + kernel relay for low-latency INT8/FP8 serving
author: Priya Reddy
description: Motivation: reduce end-to-end token latency for small-batch streaming workloads by minimizing memory traffic and branch mispredictions in the INT8/FP8 inference path. Summary: implement a compact hotpath that inlines dequantization into select attention and feed-forward microkernels, introduces a tiny relay stage to forward quantized metadata to the kernel without materializing dequant tensors, and hooks the KV-cache prefetcher to materialize only the currently needed KV window. Changes include a new IR pass (CompactDequantInline), kernel signatures that accept packed scale/zero-point hints, a lightweight per-stream relay buffer, and scheduler hints to keep hotpath lanes resident on the same worker thread. Testing: unit tests for the IR pass and kernel ABI changes; microbench harness comparing 1-8 token batch latencies across A100/RTX workloads; integration test exercising continuous batching with streaming TTFB targets. Rollout plan: default OFF; gated by the runtime config key runtime.hotpath.compact_dequant and opt-in on Dedicated for two weeks; canary traffic via rollout policy to 5% then 25% then 100%. Backwards compatibility: provides adapter when kernels are not available; falls back to existing dequant+kernel path. Checklist: - implement IR pass and codegen; - update kernel ABI and add validation tests; - update kv prefetch windowing; - add CI microbench step; - document runtime flag and rollout notes. Related: ENG-4872 (low-latency small-batch streaming), ENG-4901 (kv cache windowing improvements).
commits: Add CompactDequantInline IR pass and tests
Introduce packed-metadata ABI and kernel shims
Wire per-stream relay buffer and scheduler hints
KV window prefetch integration and adapter for fallback
review_comments: Jonas Park (review): Overall looks promising. Please add a safety net so the relay buffer cannot grow unbounded under pathological streaming clients.
Priya Reddy (reply): Added a bounded LRU-like eviction for relay entries and a per-stream max size config (runtime.hotpath.relay_max_entries).
Eleni Papadopoulos (review): The packed-metadata ABI is clever but needs a clear backwards compatibility test when older kernels are present on Dedicated nodes.
Priya Reddy (reply): Added an adapter layer and a unit test that simulates an older kernel returning EINVAL so runtime falls back to the legacy path; documented behavior in the ops doc.
Miguel Santana (review): Microbench artifacts show 8-12% p50 latency improvement on small batches; can we add a cost model note for token billing changes?
Priya Reddy (reply): Added a short note in docs/ops and a console flag to surface estimated token CPU/GPU savings for canary users.
Eleni Papadopoulos (approval): Approving pending CI-green and the relay bounds change.
CI (bot): One flaky test in bench microbench harness; reran and all green.
release_notes: Runtime: add compact dequant hotpath that inlines dequant into selected attention/FFN kernels to reduce memory traffic and p50/p95 latency for small-batch streaming workloads; gated behind runtime.hotpath.compact_dequant and off by default; KV cache prefetch windowing integrated to avoid unnecessary materialization; rollout controlled via canary.
notes_for_ops: Default disabled; to enable on Dedicated set runtime.hotpath.compact_dequant=true and configure runtime.hotpath.relay_max_entries; monitor runtime.hotpath.hotpath_lane_misses and kv.prefetch.materialization metrics. If unexpected fallbacks observed, check kernel ABI compatibility logs (hotpath.abadapter.warn).
performance_summary: Local microbench (A100): 1-token batch p50 -12%, p95 -8%; 4-token batch p50 -9%; throughput unchanged for large batches. Memory traffic to global dequant buffers reduced by ~40% for hotpathed models.
extra_context: This PR was driven by customer SUP-1198 where a payments product observed high TTFB for streaming completion endpoints; compact hotpath reduces tail latency without changing model outputs.
